title: Reusing Trajectories in Policy Gradients Enables Fast Convergence
claim: Combining past trajectories with current ones through a single multiple-importance-weighting estimator reuses stored data across iterations instead of discarding it.
layout: Single panel, left-to-right, dashed history box feeding an orange estimator box
description: A single diagram of the update scheme up to iteration k=2. A dashed gray rounded box labeled 'History H_2' contains four rounded nodes in a 2x2 grid. The top row holds the parameters θ1 and θ2, and the bottom row holds the trajectories τ1 and τ2. Black arrows show the update dynamics, θ1→θ2 and τ1→θ2. Blue arrows show trajectory sampling, θ1→τ1 and θ2→τ2. Three orange arrows come out of the box, from θ2, τ2 and τ1 (a long curved arrow). They all point to a light-orange box on the right containing the MIW gradient estimator ∇̂₂^MIW J(θ2). The eye goes first to the orange estimator box, then back along the arrows to the history.
caption: Update scheme up to $k=2$. Arrows denote: (\textcolor{ibmUltramarine}{\rule[0.5ex]{0.25cm}{1pt}}) trajectory sampling, (\textcolor{black}{\rule[0.5ex]{0.25cm}{1pt}}) update dynamics, and (\textcolor{ibmOrange}{\rule[0.5ex]{0.25cm}{1pt}}) estimator inputs.
abstract: Policy gradient (PG) methods are a class of effective reinforcement learning algorithms, particularly when dealing with continuous control problems. They rely on fresh on-policy data, making them sample-inefficient and requiring $O(Îµ^{-2})$ trajectories to reach an $Îµ$-approximate stationary point. A common strategy to improve efficiency is to reuse information from past iterations, such as previous gradients or trajectories, leading to off-policy PG methods. While gradient reuse has received substantial attention, leading to improved rates up to $O(Îµ^{-3/2})$, the reuse of past trajectories, although intuitive, remains largely unexplored from a theoretical perspective. In this work, we provide the first rigorous theoretical evidence that reusing past off-policy trajectories can significantly accelerate PG convergence. We propose RT-PG (Reusing Trajectories - Policy Gradient), a novel algorithm that leverages a power mean-corrected multiple importance weighting estimator to effectively combine on-policy and off-policy data coming from the most recent $Ï$ iterations. Through a novel analysis, we prove that RT-PG achieves a sample complexity of $\tilde{O}(Îµ^{-2}Ï^{-1})$. When reusing all available past trajectories, this leads to a rate of $\tilde{O}(Îµ^{-1})$, the best known one in the literature for PG methods. We further validate our approach empirically, demonstrating its effectiveness against baselines with state-of-the-art rates.
